messages:
Alex: Heads-up — we just saw a spike in schema validation errors for the external tool adapter (tool_x). Lots of calls returning `[]` instead of the expected `{result: ...}` and it’s triggering the degen route + retries. ~3% of calls in the last 15m. Logs: ```ERROR validate: expected object, got array -> trace=aa12f; payload=[ ]```
Mei: Ugh. Any idea whether these are real downstream regressions or a deserialization edgecase?
Alex: Quick grep shows most traces come from our autocomplete flow (short context). The tool sometimes returns an empty array when nothing to return. Historically we coerced but the strict validator started rejecting.
Jamal: Is the validator the same one used in the canary strict rollout? I thought we only enabled strict for 5% traffic.
Sara: It is. The canary toggle flipped last night (rollout step 2). This surge looks like noise exposed by strict validation.
Mei: Can we add a tolerant-parser fallback before routing to degen? Something like: if body is array and length == 0 -> map to { result: null, _coerced: true } and mark telemetry.
Jamal: I worry about silent coercion causing customer app bugs. If we coerce, we should tag the response and increment a new metric so we can roll back quickly.
Sara: Agree — no silent fixes. We need: (1) a coercion flag in the response header, (2) a sample stored payload for later inspection, (3) separate metric (tool_x.coercion_count).
Alex: Proposed quick patch: add soft-accept path behind a feature flag 'fncall-coerce-empty-array', default OFF. When ON for X% traffic, coerce and emit telemetry with reason="empty_array" and trace id.
Mei: That works. Also add a console alert and dashboard graph for coercion_count vs strict_rejects so PMs can correlate.
Jamal: Minor: what about billing attribution? If the request gets routed to degen variant (longer path) we might overbill. We should ensure coercion happens before routing decision to avoid extra cost.
Sara: Good catch. The validator lives in the routing layer now, so coercion must run before route selection. If we implement in adapter after routing it’s too late.
Alex: I'll push a patch that moves the tolerant check into the routing preprocessor. POC snippet: ```python
# routing preproc
if body_type == 'array' and len(body)==0:
  out = {"result": None, "_coerced": True}
  telemetry.increment('tool_x.coercion_count', tags={"reason":"empty_array"})
  mark_header('X-Fncall-Coerced','true')
  return out
```
Mei: Add a sampling hook so we only persist full payloads for e.g. 1% of coerced hits to keep storage sane: `telemetry.sample_store(payload, sample_rate=0.01)`.
Jamal: For rollout plan: enable feature flag for 0.1% -> monitor coercion_count, strict_rejects, QA evals on sample set -> bump to 1% -> if good, add to 10% and start deprecation of strict-block path.
Sara: Also create a dashboard card in Redwood Console: "Fncall: Tool X Empty-Array Coercions" with links to sampled traces and a button to toggle the flag (ops-only).
Alex: I'll own the change. Making a ticket: RW-12543. Will open PR and include unit tests for empty array, single-item array, and object passthrough.
Mei: Tests should assert header X-Fncall-Coerced when coerced, and no header when not. Also add a lint rule to prevent swallowing other array shapes.
Jamal: One more: add an alert burn-in that fires if coercion_count / total_calls > 0.5% for 5m during rollout. If triggered, auto-disable flag and notify #eng-oncall.
ops-bot: deploy-bot triggered deploy RW/patch/6789 -> environment=canary -> status=started :rocket:
Alex: Thanks. I'll draft the PR and the console card mock. Targeting canary toggle today, 0.1% first.
Sara: Good plan. Tag me on the PR for the dashboard bits.
Mei: I'll add sampling + persistence helpers in telemetry lib.
Jamal: I'll own oncall runbook update (how to interpret coercion vs true downstream change).
Alex: Final note — don't forget to add a deprecation note in the model adapters doc: older adapters may return arrays; we should encourage object-shaped responses.
Sara: Cool. Follow-ups: RW-12543 (Alex), RW-12544 (Mei telemetry), RW-12545 (Jamal oncall), RW-12546 (Sara console).
Alex: Closing the loop — will post PR link in this thread when ready. :thumbsup:
